transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this... this heavy mix of fear and guilt. It's like I'm tense all day, just waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't get out of your head?

Yeah, I do. Um, it happens a lot when I'm working. I'll just be doing my job, measuring a railing or maybe I'll hear a ladder scrape against a wall, and out of nowhere, I can see my husband falling. It's... it's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops, and my hands get shaky. It's really hard to get the image to stop once it starts.
Are these repetitive thoughts and images of your husband falling always triggered by something, like the sounds you mentioned, or do they happen randomly as well?

Well, like I was just saying, it definitely happens a lot with those specific triggers at work, like the ladder scraping. But... yeah, it happens randomly, too. 

I could just be sitting at home or driving, and out of nowhere, that exact same image of him falling just flashes in my head. It doesn't always take a specific sound to set it off. And whenever it happens, even if it's random, it brings on that exact same reaction... my stomach drops and my hands get shaky all over again.
How long have you been experiencing these intrusive images and feelings of fear and guilt?
It's been about four months now. Basically, it started right after it happened... ever since his fall when we were doing that porch repair.
Have these experiences and feelings been affecting your ability to work or interact with others?

Well, I'm still working, but... it's definitely having an impact. My inspection reports are taking a lot longer to finish because I just keep second-guessing everything I write down. And I've actually been turning down jobs that involve elevated decks or porches. I used to handle those without any hesitation at all, but now... I just can't bring myself to do them.
Have you been avoiding places, people, or activities outside of work because of what happened to your husband?

Like I mentioned a minute ago, I've definitely started turning down jobs with raised porches or second-story decks. But outside of work... yeah, it happens at home, too. 

I find excuses not to talk about the repair at all with my husband. And I avoid even looking at the spot where it happened... I just try to steer clear of that part of the yard entirely so I don't have to see it.
Are there any specific people you've been avoiding talking to about your husband's fall?
No, not really. I mean, besides my husband, there isn't really anyone else I'm actively avoiding talking to about it. I just try to keep it to myself, mostly.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your husband's fall?

No, not really. I still like doing the things I normally do. I mean... I still enjoy my hobbies and just relaxing, stuff like that. It hasn't really affected my interest in everyday things, just... you know, the specific things I mentioned before.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of your husband's fall is something you do most of the time, or is it something you're able to control or overcome occasionally?

I would say it's pretty much most of the time. I don't really try to overcome it... it's just easier to avoid the porch jobs and stay away from that side of the yard. I don't really see a reason to force myself to deal with it if I don't have to.
Have you noticed any decrease in your interest in activities you used to find enjoyable since your husband's fall?

I think you actually just asked me that a minute ago. But no, I really haven't noticed any decrease. Like I was saying before, I still enjoy all my usual hobbies and everything. My interest in everyday things is completely normal, it's really just the stuff around the porch that I'm staying away from.
Are there any activities that you used to find very enjoyable before your husband's fall, but now you don't find as enjoyable?

I feel like we keep coming back to this. No, there really aren't. Like I mentioned just a minute ago, I still enjoy everything I used to. I haven't lost interest in any of my hobbies or anything else. It's really just the porch I avoid.
Have you felt less interested in social activities or spending time with friends and family since your husband's fall?
No, not at all. I know we've kind of touched on this already, but my social life is exactly the same as it was. I still see my friends, still spend time with family... none of that has changed.
Are there any activities that you have completely stopped doing since your husband's fall?

Well, like I've been saying, it really just comes back to the porch. I'm a building inspector, and I guess I have completely stopped doing certain types of inspections. I've started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. I just won't take them right now. And at home... I basically find excuses not to talk about the repair work, and I definitely avoid looking at the spot where he fell. So I haven't stopped my normal life, just anything related to that kind of structure or that specific spot.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back from or feeling less invested in your hobbies or other activities you normally enjoy, compared to before your husband's fall?

No, I haven't. I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit here, but... no, I haven't pulled back from my hobbies at all. I'm still just as invested in the things I do for fun as I was before the fall. That part of my life hasn't really changed.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of your husband's fall is causing significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Well, it's definitely affecting my work. Like I mentioned, I'm still working, but... I've been turning down those elevated deck or porch jobs that I used to handle without hesitation. And even with the jobs I do take, my inspection reports are taking a lot longer because I just keep second-guessing myself. So, yeah, it's causing some issues there.
Are there any activities that you used to find very enjoyable before your husband's fall, but now you find you have little to no interest in doing?

No, not at all. Like I was just saying, I haven't really lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. The things I enjoyed doing before, I still enjoy doing them now. It's really just those specific situations with the decks and porches that I'm avoiding, but my interest in the fun stuff hasn't dropped off.
Are there any activities that you have completely lost interest in since your husband's fall?
No, there really isn't. I feel like we're kind of going in circles with this, but no, I haven't lost interest in any of my activities. I'm still doing all the same things I used to do.
Have you noticed yourself having less interest in activities that you used to find very enjoyable, such as hobbies, since your husband's fall?

I know we just went over this, but no. I really haven't noticed any change with my hobbies or the things I do for fun. I still enjoy them just as much as I did before. It's really just those specific work situations I mentioned earlier that are bothering me.
